sections.h2: Which Spalding County offices touch a tax bill?
sections.html:
Spalding County divides the work among five bodies. The Tax Commissioner owns the bill and the payment window. The assessors value property and approve exemptions, and a Grand Jury appointed board of equalization settles disputes. Millage rates come from the commissioners and the school board.

The Tax Commissioner's office moved to 411 E. Solomon Street in Griffin, three blocks from the courthouse. The phone is (770) 467-4360 and the mailbox is PO Box 509, Griffin, GA 30224. Call (770) 467-4240 for the Tax Assessor. County administration works from 119 E. Solomon Street.

sections.h2: What is the November deadline in Spalding County, and what do late payers owe?
sections.html:
Bills for land, buildings and business equipment normally fall due on November 15. The Tax Commissioner says late fees do not start until 60 days after the bills go out. After the due date the county adds interest monthly at the legal rate, and a 5% penalty accrues every 120 days up to 20%.

Homesteaded property owing under $500 escapes the penalty. Mobile homes sit on an April 1 schedule with a location permit, and the office can levy on unpaid property as a last resort.

sections.h2: What are the key Spalding County tax rules at a glance?
sections.html:
Spalding County property tax rules, from the Spalding County Tax Commissioner's website
TopicRule as the county prints it
Assessed value40% of fair market value
Return seasonOpens January 1 and closes April 1
Land and building billsDue November 15
Appeal cutoffForty-five days after the notice mailing date
Homestead filingApplication in hand before April 1 earns the exemption for that tax year
Mobile home taxDue April 1
Delinquent tax salesHeld on a first Tuesday, 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

A mill is one thousandth of a dollar per dollar of assessed value. The county's order of operations is to subtract exemptions from the 40% assessed value first and apply the millage rate to what remains.

sections.h2: What is the route for contesting a Spalding County value?
sections.html:
Owners in Spalding County have forty-five days after the assessment notice goes out. The county's FAQ says to argue taxability, value or uniformity, and to leave the size of the bill out of it. The assessors review first; the next stops are the equalization board or arbitration, then Superior Court.

For tax year 2026, the county Tax Commissioner stretched the homestead filing window to match the appeal period, June 5 through July 23, 2026, and that period has ended. Exemptions based on income had to be requested in person with proof of 2025 income.

sections.h2: Which homestead exemptions does Spalding County offer?
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner lists state and local exemptions combined. The main ones:

  • Standard homestead: $2,000 each from the state, county and school portions, with no income test.
  • Standard elderly: age 65 before January 1, net income capped at $15,000, with bigger county and school deductions.
  • School exemption: age 62 or older, or totally disabled at any age, with household gross income capped at $12,500.
  • Ages 65 to 69, $10,000 off the school portion regardless of income; ages 70 to 74, $20,000; ages 75 and older, $30,000.
  • A floating school exemption for owners 65 and up, which freezes the value used for school tax.

An approved exemption carries forward until the owner moves, so a buyer applies fresh for the new address. Owners 62 and up with household income below $15,000 may have a deferral on file; the Tax Commissioner can confirm for your parcel.

sections.h2: What does the Census show for Spalding County sellers?
sections.html:
Census figures for Spalding County show 70,775 people in mid-2025, a 5.2% rise from the 2020 base, living among 29,850 housing units. The middle home value is $228,700 and owners occupy 62.7% of housing units. Gross rent runs about $1,113 a month at the median, and median household income is $62,071. Roughly one resident in five (20.6%) is 65 or older, which puts the senior exemptions above in play for many sellers.

The county covers 195.97 square miles of land with 343.5 people per square mile, and Griffin is where the courthouse, tax office and clerk all sit. The county's own news page notes a comprehensive plan update that looks toward 2050 and the county commissioners' adoption of a full rollback rate for 2025, which can come up in buyer conversations.

sections.h2: Which other Spalding County notices could affect a house sale?
sections.html:
The county home page carries several items a seller may want to read. Spalding approved zoning code changes that sit in a separate section of its online code until a full zoning rewrite is adopted in 2026, and a comprehensive plan update will guide growth through 2050. The county reports it moved up to a Tier 2 ranking in Georgia's 2026 Job Tax Credit rankings, which it ties to better employment and income measures.

The Georgia Department of Transportation held a public open house in Griffin on May 7, 2026 about replacing the State Route 16 bridge over the Norfolk Southern Railroad, with comments accepted through May 21, 2026. A house near that corridor may draw questions from buyers. Heirs selling an inherited house can reach the county Probate Court at (770) 467-4341.

sections.h2: How are delinquent taxes and tax sales handled in Spalding County?
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner's FAQ explains that Georgia law puts delinquent tax sales on a month's first Tuesday, within a 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. window. The sale takes place at 411 E. Solomon Street. Bidder rules on the Tax Commissioner's site:

  • Register on sale morning between 8:00 and 9:30.
  • Be at least 18 years old.
  • Show a driver's license or other official ID.

Bidding usually starts around 10:00 or 10:30.

Notices run in the Griffin Daily News on Tuesdays starting four weeks before a sale, and the office posts the sale list on its site. Excess funds requests for tax sale proceeds need original documents, and the office accepts no email. If a house you own faces a sale, contact the Tax Commissioner before the advertising starts.

sections.h2: Where do I record the deed or get a copy in Spalding County?
sections.html:
The Clerk of Superior Court keeps deeds, at 132 E. Solomon Street in Griffin. Call 770-467-4309 to reach the clerk, whose staff includes a deputy for real estate. The Tax Commissioner's FAQ sends owners to this office for a copy of a warranty deed.

Spalding County's Community Development department at 119 E. Solomon Street covers planning, zoning and permits for unincorporated Spalding County. The Planning Commission gathers on the last Tuesday evening of each month, and the Board of Appeals follows on the second Thursday, both at 6:00 p.m. in the Courthouse Annex. Call the department before you start repair work if the house sits outside the city of Griffin. Its contact list also names a business and alcohol license technician and a permit technician, so ask for the right desk when you call.

faqs.q: What is the Spalding County payment deadline?
faqs.a: November 15, for bills on land, buildings and business personal property. Late fees wait until 60 days after the bills are mailed.

faqs.q: What is the appeal cutoff after a Spalding County assessment notice?
faqs.a: Forty-five days after the notice is mailed. Assessors review first, then the equalization board or an arbitrator, and finally Superior Court.

faqs.q: What is the Spalding County late penalty?
faqs.a: Once November 15 passes, interest accrues each month, and penalties climb in 5% steps every 120 days to 20%. Homesteaded parcels with less than $500 due skip the penalty.

faqs.q: Where is the Spalding County Tax Commissioner's office?
faqs.a: 411 E. Solomon Street in Griffin, GA 30223, phone (770) 467-4360. It opens at 8:00 on weekdays and closes at 4:30.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Spalding County house that owes back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, though the Tax Commissioner can levy on unpaid property and sell it at a tax sale. Request a payoff figure that includes interest and penalties so the balance can be settled from your closing proceeds.
